Member-only story

The company is telling the world that AI is its “most important priority.” It is also firing the people who actually build it.

6 min read
Just now

--

Press enter or click to view image in full size

On July 22, 2026, Amazon quietly confirmed that it had laid off an undisclosed number of employees from its Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) organization.
No public announcement. No press conference. No CEO blog post with carefully rehearsed empathy. Just a confirmation to reporters after Reuters broke the story.
The official line? Amazon is “sharpening its focus on the initiatives that matter most for customers.”
Translation: we are cutting the people who do research and doubling down on the people who generate revenue.

Let that contradiction sit for a moment. Because this is not just an Amazon story. This is the story of what happens when the entire tech industry realizes that spending billions on AI does not automatically produce billions in return.
